edges.description: Loss of IL-36 receptor antagonist function permits unopposed IL-36 inflammatory signaling.
Sterile pustules are neutrophils recruited into the epidermis by unopposed IL-36 signalling — the pus is the mechanism made visible, not infection.
Widespread erythema accompanying the pustular eruption.
Sheet-like scaling as the affected epidermis is shed.
Systemic inflammation during flares; generalised pustular psoriasis is a systemic illness rather than a skin-limited one.
The acute-phase marker tracking flare activity.
Serum CRP reflects the systemic inflammation driven by the IL-36 axis during flares.

evidence.snippet: BACKGROUND: Generalized pustular psoriasis is a life-threatening disease of unknown cause. It is characterized by sudden, repeated episodes of high-grade fever, generalized rash, and disseminated pustules, with hyperleukocytosis and elevated serum levels of C-reactive protein, which may be associated with plaque-type psoriasis.

evidence.snippet: These findings suggest loss of function of IL36RN as the genetic basis of GPP and implicate innate immune dysregulation in this severe episodic inflammatory disease, thereby highlighting IL-1 signaling as a potential target for therapeutic intervention.
